fields.Text: Entity names should be all {{c1::singular}} (preferred) or all plural, but never {{c2::mixed}}.

fields.Front: In which directions should relationships read on an ER diagram?
fields.Back: Left to right and top to bottom, using meaningful names.

fields.Front: What is wrong with the diagram PATIENT --- Treats --- DOCTORS --- Is employee by --- NURSE?
fields.Back: 'Doctors' is plural while others are singular; 'Treats' reads backwards (should be IS TREATED BY); 'Is employee by' is wrong and reads backwards (should be EMPLOYS).

fields.Front: What are the cardinalities of Patient IS TREATED BY Doctor and Doctor EMPLOYS Nurse (speaker notes)?
fields.Back: Patient-Doctor: many to many. Doctor-Nurse: one to many.

fields.Front: What kinds of names does the instructor tell you to avoid?
fields.Back: Meaningless names like 'item one' or 'object two'; use meaningful names.

fields.Front: Is reading left-to-right and top-to-bottom mandatory?
fields.Back: No: 'if possible... it's not a big deal if you can't'. It just makes the diagram easier to explain to users. Singular names, however, are required in this course.

fields.Text: Case study: 'Department works for employee' reads badly, so the instructor renames the relationship '{{c1::has}}' (department has employee).

fields.Front: Give two ways to fix 'Patient treats Doctor'.
fields.Back: Rename the relationship IS TREATED BY, or swap the positions of DOCTOR and PATIENT so 'treats' reads left to right.

fields.Front: In the doctor's-office practice example, what participation did the instructor assign to Doctor EMPLOYS Nurse?
fields.Back: Total on both sides: every doctor has a nurse helping them and every nurse works for some doctor; one doctor per nurse assuming a single-doctor office.
